raw_response:
I’m still doing cotton this year on all 9 mu. I’ve grown it many years, and at my age I don’t want to change to something unfamiliar. Cotton is slower to get money back, but I know how to manage it, and with our well I can still hold it through a dry spell. I don’t read those technical things, so I mostly do what has worked on my land. If I save too much on fertilizer, the plants stay weak and the bolls don’t set well, so I’d rather put a solid base amount and then watch the field. But money is still money, so I won’t push inputs too hard. I’ll plant around mid to late April, use the hybrid seed the local sellers usually carry, put fertilizer in before planting and once more when the plants are growing strong, irrigate a couple of times if rain is short, and spray only when I really see weeds or insects. I’ll keep tillage simple, use family labor first, and hire a little help only around the busy picking time.
